title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the opening page of Grothendieck's May 1966 letter to John Tate from Pisa, the founding document of crystalline ideas. He says the letter grew out of thinking about formal groups (their Dieudonné theory) and de Rham cohomology. The aim is a characteristic-free, intrinsic de Rham-type theory, and a Dieudonné theory of formal and p-divisible groups via crystals.

Setup (1.0). R is a base prescheme (mostly Spec Z) and S is an R-prescheme. C is the category of R-preschemes T under S, meaning they carry an R-morphism i: S -> T. The map i must be a closed immersion defined by a locally nilpotent ideal, so T is a nilpotent thickening of S with the same underlying space. Morphisms in C are R-morphisms T -> T' compatible with the maps from S.

The forgetful functor C -> (Sch) pulls back the fibred category of quasi-coherent modules. This gives a fibred category over C whose fibre at T is QCoh(T).

Definition 1.1. A crystal of (quasi-coherent) modules on S relative to R is a cartesian section of this fibred category. Concretely it consists of:
- for each thickening T, a quasi-coherent O_T-module M_T;
- for each morphism f: T -> T' in C, an isomorphism f^*M_{T'} ≅ M_T;
- these isomorphisms satisfy the cocycle condition.

More generally, for any fibred category F over (Sch)/R, an F-crystal is a cartesian section of F pulled back to C. This covers crystals of algebras, of commutative algebras, of relative schemes, and so on. When R = Spec Z these are called 'absolute' crystals.

1.2. F-crystals form a category functorial in F. Hence tensor operations on crystals of modules are defined termwise and satisfy the usual identities.

In modern terms this is the infinitesimal site (without topology and without divided powers). A crystal is a quasi-coherent crystal on Inf(S/R), with global rather than Zariski-local thickenings; this is harmless because thickenings are topologically trivial. For S smooth over R in characteristic 0, such crystals are equivalent to quasi-coherent modules with integrable connection (stratifications). Divided powers, which are needed for good behaviour in characteristic p, do not yet appear on this page.
errors: No mathematical error. Divided powers are absent, so this notion is the infinitesimal (not crystalline) one, which behaves badly in characteristic p (infinitesimal cohomology is not the right p-adic theory). Grothendieck himself later introduced PD-thickenings; this is a limitation of the definition at this stage, not an error.
Minor slip in the retyped version (next page), 1.2: 'cristaux de modules sur C' should be 'sur S', as on this page. Typo 'De Rahm' for 'De Rham'.

ideas.what: Category C of nilpotent thickenings of S over R, used as a 'site' for de Rham-type theory
ideas.modern_name: infinitesimal site Inf(S/R) (precursor of the crystalline site)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1966 letter to Tate; 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', 1968)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (notes by Coates–Jussila), in Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas (1968)

ideas.what: Crystal as a cartesian section of a fibred category over the category of thickenings (rigidity plus growth)
ideas.modern_name: crystal (of quasi-coherent modules) on the infinitesimal site
ideas.where_published: Dix exposés (1968); the letter to Tate itself is known and circulated

ideas.what: F-crystals for an arbitrary fibred category F (crystals of algebras, schemes, etc.)
ideas.modern_name: crystals in a fibred category / stack
ideas.where_published: Dix exposés (1968); Grothendieck, Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné (Montréal 1970)

ideas.what: Tensor operations on crystals induced functorially from operations on F
ideas.modern_name: tensor structure on the category of crystals

deep.surprise_reason: This is the famous, well-known letter to Tate introducing crystals. Its content was published in essence in Dix exposés (1968) and developed by Berthelot, and the letter itself circulates. Nothing on this opening page is absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'R-[-??-]morphisme': the image shows overtyped letters, apparently a typed 'R-homomorphisme' corrected to 'R-morphisme' (cf. next page '[-m-]').
The section number appears handwritten as '1.-' or '1.o', not clearly '1.0'.
'De Rahm' is Grothendieck's own typo in the original (corrected to 'De Rham' in the retyped version).
Header: the faint letterhead (Università di Pisa, Istituto Matematico 'Leonida Tonelli') shows through reversed from the back of the sheet, and there is a handwritten page number '1'.
